rules.statement: Do not force-synthesize `auth_time` into access tokens; include it only when the authenticated principal actually carries it.
rules.why: RFC 9068 says `auth_time` goes in the access token only when available, so always synthesizing it is the wrong default.
rules.check: Look for access-token claim building that adds `auth_time` from a fallback source (for example, the cookie's IssuedUtc) when the principal has no real `auth_time` claim.

rules.statement: Always include `auth_time` in the ID token when it is required (a `max_age` request was made, or `auth_time` was requested as an essential claim), whatever optional-inclusion setting is in effect, and limit any fallback synthesis of `auth_time` to that required case.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 makes `auth_time` mandatory only in these cases and optional otherwise, so synthesizing it every time goes beyond the spec, and dropping it when required breaks the spec.
rules.check: Check that ID-token issuance calculates whether `auth_time` is required from `max_age` or essential claim requests and honors that even when the include-by-default toggle is off, and that synthesis code runs only when the claim is required and missing.

rules.statement: Do not hardcode `acr` values at login. Resolve `acr` through a replaceable, DI-overridable service whose honest default leaves the claim out unless the methods performed or a configured baseline justify a value.
rules.why: OpenID Connect defers the meaning of `acr` values to the deployment, so a hardcoded value invents a policy decision that deployments cannot cleanly override.
rules.check: Look for literal `acr` values (for example "1", "2", or LoA numbers) assigned directly in authentication or token code instead of coming from a resolver service or configuration.

rules.statement: Record authentication-event properties (`amr`, `acr`, `auth_time`, `idp`) when authentication happens, have the component that performed the authentication set its own `amr`, and store these values on the principal and session instead of deriving them later at token issuance.
rules.why: These values describe the authentication event, and only the authenticating component knows which methods it used. Recording them once keeps them consistent for the whole session.
rules.check: Look for new authentication entry points (sign-in, ROPC, external login) that don't stamp `amr` and the resolved `acr` on the principal and session, and for token issuance code that computes `acr` from `amr` after the fact.

rules.statement: Make an extensibility service interface async from the start if a replacement implementation could reasonably need IO.
rules.why: A real replacement may need a database or external lookup, and switching a synchronous signature to async later is a breaking change.
rules.check: Look for new public interfaces meant to be replaced (policy or resolver seams) that use synchronous method signatures even though plausible implementations would do IO.

rules.statement: Register default implementations of replaceable services with `TryAdd*`, such as `TryAddSingleton`, so applications can override them through DI.
rules.why: The default must be replaceable by a deployment's own registration without having to remove or fight the library's registration.
rules.check: Look for default implementations of extensibility interfaces registered with `Add*` instead of `TryAdd*` in service-collection extension methods.

rules.statement: When an `acr` claim is requested as essential with specific `values` and the principal's `acr` satisfies none of them, deny with `access_denied`. Handle voluntary `acr` requests, including the `acr_values` parameter, on a best-effort basis without denying.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.5.1.1 requires essential `acr` values to be enforced, while voluntary requests are only hints.
rules.check: Check that subject-authentication validation compares an essential `id_token.acr` request's values with the principal's `acr` and returns `access_denied` when none match, and that it does not reject requests that are only voluntary.
